title: Higher-order function types and callbacks
hook: Higher-order function types and callbacks shows up in everyday TypeScript and in senior interviews — this page explains what it is, why it matters, and how it behaves in the compiler versus JavaScript or C#.

blocks.text: Higher-order function types and callbacks is a core concept in TypeScript. At run time, types erase — the engine still executes JavaScript — but at compile time this concept shapes safe APIs and catches bugs before deploy. This page explains the idea in plain English first, then shows small, explained examples you can run in the browser console or Node.js.

entries.plainDefinition: The official specification that JavaScript implements. TypeScript is a typed superset that compiles to ECMAScript.

blocks.text: Senior interviews and production code both probe whether you understand Higher-order function types and callbacks beyond syntax memorization. Misunderstanding here leads to subtle bugs — wrong equality results, leaked memory, untyped JSON boundaries, or async ordering surprises. If you know JavaScript, the comparison sections below help you transfer mental models instead of starting from zero.

blocks.title: Interview trap
blocks.body: Interviewers often ask "Higher-order function types and callbacks" as a follow-up to a coding exercise. They want mechanism and tradeoffs — not a one-line definition.
